findings.rule: data integrity of exported files; round-1 ExportDirectory finding (one file per application); cross-lane #280 file card Share/Open and #283 file-name setting
findings.trigger: Files are keyed only by the ExportFileName string, which is not unique per application: NAME_RESUME gives every application 'Priya-Deshmukh_Resume.pdf' (and NAME_ROLE / NAME_COMPANY_ROLE collide for two jobs with the same title, or the same company and title). #283 Settings cycles to NAME_RESUME. (1) Overwrite: export A, then export B under NAME_RESUME; B's rename replaces A's PDF, and A.exportFileName still names it, so #280 Application detail Share for A (and ExportedViewModel.resolveFile / storedExport, which read by name) sends B's resume, tailored to another job, with A's page count. (2) Delete: then switch to NAME_ROLE and re-export A; previousFileName 'Priya-Deshmukh_Resume.pdf' != new name, so line 19 deletes B's current file and B's Share shows 'Couldn't find the PDF'. Smallest fix that keeps the visible file name: write each application's PDF in its own folder, exports/<applicationId>/<fileName> (cache-path exports/ already covers subfolders; sign-out deleteRecursively already removes them), and give ExportedFileStore.fileFor the applicationId. Adding an id suffix to the name would also work but changes the name the employer sees; 'never delete a name another application references' fixes only case 2.
findings.title: Applications that share an export file name overwrite or delete each other's PDF
findings.proof: ExportResumeUseCaseTest: settings NAME_RESUME, seed accepted applications app-1 and app-2 with different bullets, export app-1 then app-2; expect app-1's stored file to still hold app-1's render (fails at head: both resolve to the same path, last writer wins).

findings.rule: 279-c7 and round-1 credits finding: the credits line must describe the spend for this application; billing copy must be true
findings.trigger: fundedByFree is set true by any free SPEND of the application and never reset, so it describes the first tailoring, not the latest. Ledger FREE_GRANT +1, SPEND -1 (app X, free), PURCHASE +5, SPEND -1 (app X, a second run: #277 JobResult 'Tailor' calls navigateToTailoring with a new runId, and #280 adds 'Re-tailor with profile changes · 1 credit'). Export X: the walk returns true, the card shows the big 4 and 'Free resume used. Nothing was charged.' although this tailoring cost a paid credit. Fix: assign instead of latch, fundedByFree = (freeUsed == cost) for each SPEND of this application, so the last one wins. On w4-base this when statement also stops compiling (non-exhaustive over REFUND and MIGRATION, an error since Kotlin 1.7); add those branches (REFUND/MIGRATION -> Unit keeps the copy true: they never make a spend free).
findings.title: Free line latches on the application's first spend, so a paid re-tailor still says 'Nothing was charged'
findings.proof: ExportedViewModelTest: ledger FREE_GRANT 1, SPEND -1 app-1, PURCHASE 5, SPEND -1 app-1 (later createdAt); expect freeResumeUsed == false (fails at head).
